items.title: Nepal review and back to Kathmandu 12/22
items.body:
Last night was the first time we encountered someone who needed punched in the face. There were several guys staying at The Family House who were drunk. Andy got up to see what was going on since they were arguing w our host Govinder. Luckily he didn't have to intervene. They acted up again early in the am. Not sure how I slept for most of the 12 hours I was in bed. 

We had a breakfast, I had a great bowl of muesli w yogurt and bananas, Andy had toast w butter (ghee eww) and jelly and we had boiled eggs and masala tea. These eggs are wonderful, can't get enough. We walk to the bus stop was a freakin commercial. Picture this: two backpackers walking down a country road, the fog in the sky, the sun rising casts a beautiful hue over the fields of mustard. Children yell at us from their houses and we exchange "namaste", "hello", and "goodbye"s. Grandpas riding their bikes down the road greet us w more "namaste "s. A mom w two children on the back of her bike ride down the road and they all smile and wave. The Nepalese people are the absolute nicest, and the children and sweet and adorable and have huge smiles when they see us. Parents put their small children's' hands together and say "namaste" when we walk by. So freakin cute. If I saw this in a commercial my cynical self would be like, that's BS. You see these little kids, less than 2, holding onto their parents' back on motorcycles and bicycles. Kids have amazing survival skills. 

This country is a backpackers' dream. Amazing people that are so nice and helpful (where are you going? They ask as we wander around), cheap loding and food, and the food is delicious! I haven't had a bad meal yet. I'm actually so used to not showering, it may be hard to adjust to a daily shower back home (just sayin). The people all want to engage in a conversation, even the waiters hang around us while we are eating to chat. I don't even want a bathroom w a western toilet anymore- they really don't make sense. Andy wants to put in the squat toilets in our home but I don't think that would do anything for the resale value. The people seem very happy here although they have little. The men are probably more happy because they don't do shit. Andy comments on how all the women are doing the dishes (yeah I see but we don't live here so this doesn't help your POV). It's hard to not show PDA here. It's probably not accepted because the women are working all day. 

It's hard to see the animals though. There  aren't many cats, but the dogs are treated like shit (and the elephants). Some have dogs as pets, but the strays have rocks thrown at them, and need some flea and mange meds. Yeah I get it, when the people don't have much why would the dogs, but it's still sad. Especially when I wanted to take Blackie home. 

The pollution and garbage everywhere is hard to take. People go down to the rivers to throw their garbage in. When there are so many countries in this world that don't give a shit about the environment, how can we make a difference? We are so fucked. Really fucked. You can't breathe the air in China anymore. It's not acceptable in Kathmandu either. The smaller towns are better but the burning of trash makes me sick to smell and creates smog. Mother Earth is going to bitch slap us hard. And quit using non reusable plastic! This shit is everywhere. Marina said the Congolese can't even farm because of the layer of plastic in the ground. Why use the thin shitty plastic bags? Even at home we say no to them and the response we get is "why they are free?". Not the point. Bring your own damn reusable bag. This isn't some California hippie shit. Plastic is destroying the environment and animals. We saw a cow eating a plastic bag in the city, he's a goner. 

We got stuck in gridlock. Not in the city but on the side of a mountain. A truck broke down and the trucks trying to pass (like they do) fucked it up. Actually I think it was our bus that was the cause. There was a lot of backing up and yelling and honking but we got out of the way and back in the way. Pretty funny. The tourist buses are nicer but slower. I guess they care more about killing a bus of tourists vs locals. 

The people are very resourceful. We saw large sturdy baskets made out of grasss, rebar used for bike kickstands, bamboo and old tires to make squat seats (soon to be showcased in our home in Fremont. We shipped $6 seats back home? Yes, yes we did). 

After sitting through a traffic accident, the bus climbing 3k on a windy road, we finally made it to Kathmandu 7 hours later. They drop us off somewhere in the city- absolutely no idea where- it's not the normal bus stop depot. 

We found Thamel and the old Avalon House we stayed before. Yes $12 might be pricey but they have hot water, towels, wifi, and a nice gate opener (person). We hit up Helenas again for the rooftop bar where we ate amazing paneer pakotas, veg momos, and Andy had fries chicken of course. Tonight we check each others head for bugs- we saw parents doing it to their children on the side of the road. It sounds like a good idea to us.

items.title: I touched a baby elephant 12/21
items.body:
Andy woke me up this am, it was supposed to be a sleep in kinda of day, but I guess 10 hours is enough. We walked around looking for breakfast and settled on a nicer hotel. I had French toast w honey and boiled eggs, Andy had an omelette w toast, then busted out his own peanut butter. Who does that?!

We rented some bikes to see the baby elephants at the breeding center but we were late and didn't find the center. Well head back for the afternoon event. Today was lazy. We walked a little, found the bus station out of here for tomorrow, played w a puppy, then bought a beer and the most delish local chips. We rented bikes again in the afternoon and stopped by a lovely bar by the river (w no food) for some beer. Off to the elephant breeding center. 

So I don't feel good about this "breeding center". They are only breeding them for tourists to ride on from what I can tell. They way they train them is what you would expect from a 3rd world country. Hell, maybe it's how all countries train them. Not good. We saw some elephants, several calves were w their moms. That was very cute. The elephants being chained up, not so cute. They put in electric fences so the elephants wouldn't have to be chained. Some weren't working yet. We did meet some elephants in working electric wire cages. Andy was throwing them grass for them to eat. The elephants were trying to grab the grass without touching the wire. A dude was riding another elephant around who was kicking a soccer ball. I hope it was a little fun for the elephant. A dude was riding a mother elephant in and the baby was running next to her. Right toward where we were standing. I moved to the side so I wouldn't get smashed between the baby elephant and the gate. The baby stopped and I got to pet her for a brief second. Until she contined to her cage. That part was great! The rest was sad. Don't do the elephant rides boys and girls. 

Back into town for dinner. We found a great place by the river to watch the sunset. We had grilled fished and Andy got his fried chicken. Back to the hotel and we get a first hand show of a tractor digging up tree stumps. Some little kids saw it and ran back to see the action. One of them combed over the wall where the tractor was digging while the dad was on the phone. I yelled at him to get back. The kid did but climbed back over in excitement. I yelled again. I pretty much saved that kid's life. Good times.

items.title: Rhinos!... and a tick in my eye 12/20
items.body:
Up at 6:30 for a toast and omelette breakfast before our jungle walk departure w our two guides into the Chitwan park. It was really foggy so we didn't go until 7:30. We started w a canoe ride down the river. It was pretty cool w the fog. Although you couldn't see a ton, we could see birds, an alligator, and the sun trying to push through. I couldn't tell it was a gator, it's head was barely above the water.  

We landed and walked not for very long until we saw a herd of spotted deer. There were a tons of them, the males had huge antlers. We saw tons of birds, peacocks, parakeets, Eagles, black iris, blue heron, 2 different types of kingfishers. We came across another gator and this one was out of the water w his mouth open just chillin. 



Then we saw some rhinos!! The guides spotted them across the river grazing. We had a really good view of them. The guides made sure we didn't get too close so they wouldn't charge us. The rhinos butted horns for a bit, then the male tried to mount the female! So close, one more try and it didn't work. The guides said he lost his step on the wet grass. We watched in awe for about 20 min. 



We walked all around the park and found a place next to the road for lunch. We had a packed lunch of veg noodles (they made them so damn spicy it hurt). Then we waiting for an hour hoping a tiger would cross the road, the guide saw a couple days ago. We walked through trees w lots of monkeys trying to deficate on us. So cute. 

When we were walking through the forest, there were a bunch of gnats. In our face. I thought one got caught in my eye so I tired to get it out. Finally I asked Andy for help. The guide said its a tick, use your nails. A fucking tick in my eye?! Andy didn't have nails so the guide used his (great). They like to go for warm soft spots the guide said. Ugh. Later the guide said small but poisonous (I'm pretty sure he wasn't joking). So far I can still see out of my eye, I guess the morning will tell. 

We saw on the watchtower for a bit, enjoying to view of the grasses. When we got to the top Andy saw two blacks bears. They bounced away before I could see them. The guides tracked them to the tower. They were pretty good guides.  The locals burn the grasses "in a controlled fashion" (I missed the controlled part).  They were carrying wood out of the park for fuel. The men were only carrying one log (although it was a long one). But the women were carrying heavy ass logs on their heads. These women are beasts! Same deal on the mountain. Men doing shit, women doing all the heavy lifting. Funny. 

We headed back before 5 when the park shuts down. We had to take one last boat ride across the river, right where another huge gater was chillin. I'm glad we chose the walk instead of the jeep ride. I'm not how those riders couldn't have seen all the wildlife in a loud car. Back at the same restaurant for some momos in tomatoe soup (so freakin good), fish fingers, and veg pizza. Andy is missing meat and that doesn't sound good to me at all. We get to sleep in tonight. Tomorrow, baby elephants!!

items.title: The roller coaster ride to Sauraha 12/19
items.body:
Took our time getting up this am. The bed was really hard so the sleep was shit. We had an omelette and chapati for breakfast w some marsala tea. The fog was low over the mountains which made the morning chilly, but nothing as cold as the mountains. 

We chatted w Marina some more and low and behold our dogs showed up! Blackie and whitey! Black or was so happy to see Andy she was rolling around on the ground. The innkeepers were throwing rocks at them until they realized we wanted the dogs around. Blackie is a lover and Andy loved her too. I suggested we take them home- why not? We headed back for the bus area and blackie followed us the whole way. She so scared of cars, she waits for them to pass then runs to catch up w us. 



We had to leave her (so sad) and jumped on bus #1 to reach the main road. we kept saying Chitwan and no one understood what we were saying. So jumped on a bus going south (right direction) and figured they knew where we were going. 

The ride was nuts! I sat in the back where they fit 6 instead of the allocated 5. The woman next to me was holding on for dear life. I figured she was going to puke so when the dude got up next to me, I moved over to let the new guy sit next to her. Yep, granny puked in her bags and threw them out the window. It was bumpy and swervy. At one point I was bounced 6 inches out of my seat. That hurts on an ass. Good thing I don't get carsick, but Andy does. I saw him cover his face and I knew he was in trouble. He recovered and all was well for the next 4 hours. We didn't hear the locals go "ohhh" so I guess we didn't almost die. 

There are gas cans lined up along the road waiting for gas. The places we are eating are using wood to cook food. Gas stations had so many trucks and cars lined up down the road it was ridiculous. Nepal is in dire need of the constitution to be resolved w India. 

They kicked us off the bus and we asked several locals how to get to Chitwan. We trusted what they said because we heard the same thing from multiple sources. We jumped on bus #3 to get to Tadi. Once off in Tadi, a taxi offered $7 for a ride of 8 km. hell no dude. The 4 hour ride just cost that much. We'll take the bus that's "not possible ". Then a small bus pulled up and offered us a ride for $1. We had to sit on top. No problem, we've done this before. 

We made it to Sauraha by 4:00 and are staying at a dudes place who's son lives in SF as a sushi chef. It's central so why not and $6 a night. They don't have much food because of no gas so we are next door. We grabbed a couple Everest beers, veg pakotas, and veg and non veg Dal Baht. It was delish! Off to bed early after a couple sips of our whiskey. Hehe.

items.title: Moving on from the 1% 12/18
items.body:
We took our time this am to soak in the rest of the hotel. Andy got us some croissants and lattes and we ate the rest of the chocolate cake. After we shipped some stuff back home, we jumped on the bus for Begnas Lake, just southeast of Pokhara. We opted for the $.8 bus ride instead of the $30 private driver.  It was a short easy ride and we got there in the early afternoon. 

The bus came to the end of the road. Where's the lake? Andy found a sign but there were no guesthouses by the lake.  We ended up walking several miles up and over the hill towards a resort. Andy picked up a dog along the way. She followed us the whole way and stayed on his heals. I wanted to bring her home but I guess that's not possible. She was the sweetest. It's funny how scared Nepalese are of dogs when the dogs are more scared of people. 

We saw a sign for a resort so we figured why not check it out. We walked a looong way down steps knowing damn well we'd have to hike back up. Blackie followed us like she was ours. There were no visitors at the resort and they didn't want to make a deal less than $130 a night so we moved on to a $2.5 a night. Take that suckas (after we hiked back up)! The place we found is just right for us, no more people waiting on us all the time, that's annoying. We had an amazing dinner of banana lassi's, curry fish stew, and a whole grilled fish w ginger and other spices (fresh fish from the lake). Yum! We have a great view of the lake, so quiet and calm. We watched the village kids play while the sun set. The girl who lives here, Sunitshya, speaks great English and played w my phone finding games and switching my airplane mode off (ugh). She was super sweet and tools pics of herself. 



At dark, we had another traveller come to the guesthouse. Marina is from Serbia and we chatted for hours. She's has great stories about her host families in America and her time spent working in Congo. That's the best part about staying in these less expensive places, meeting cool people. I don't know where our black dog friend went. I miss her and hope she's ok.

items.title: Bday in Pokhara 12/17
items.body:
Slept in a cush bed and it was so warm, no sleeping bag, and a fluffy pillow. What?! Andy had the hotel set up breakfast on our personal terrace. It was sunny and the lake was shining. We had mushroom omelette, rösti, watermelon mango lassis, fruit, and a latte. It was a lot of food but I did my job and finished. It was funny getting so much attention from the hotel staff. The waiter waited by us to finish, the manager came up and talked to us, we took a pic w some girl from the hotel. I had no idea this was going down so I was in my PJs not looking excellent. 

We rested and finally made it out around noon. We stopped by an art store and got some pics, we stopped by a cashmere store and got some scarves. The owners of the stores were sooo happy we bought from them. They all talked about how the earthquake and now the fuel crisis is really impacting them and the tourist industry. It's so sad. We did barter a bit, but definitely didn't take advantage of them, they are in a rough spot. 

Andy was on a mission to buy two plastic chairs all the locals sit on. This isn't something foreigners buy. We were walking toward the market and a dude was selling stuff from his bike and he had 3 chairs. We bought 2, the dude was stoked. The best part was as we were carrying the chairs, all the locals' faces lit up. We got lots of thumbs up, "those are good strong chairs", "are you buying or selling", people nodding w their approval. It was hilarious how much attention we got. I guess that's not an everyday occurrence, they were very proud. 

We stopped for Andy to get his beard trimmed and man, did the dude do a great job. The dude trimmed his beard w scissors, saved his neck and temples w a straight razor (yeah weird), sprayed water on his face and hair, put lotion on his face, oil on his head, massaged his face neck head and shoulders for 10 min, and busted out the special aftershave from a box. All of this for $3! I want a shave! A $2 tip was well deserved. 

On the way back to the hotel we stopped for some snacks and Ghorka beer and enjoyed the rest of the sun. We packed our new chairs w the warm clothes we no longer need so we can ship it home. 

Andy suggested we head to the hotel bar for a drink. Then he suggested we take the drinks upstairs, but not to our terrace, the one below. It did seem odd but whatever. When we finally went to our terrace, half of the hotel staff and managers were waiting for me w a table covered in flowers and a bday cake. They lit a candle and sang happy bday and took pics w their phones. It was cute and funny and odd all at the same time. The staff here are so sweet and giving us tons of attention which we aren't used to and don't care for, but they are so nice and adorable. You can tell this isn't stuff they do everyday as their surprise coordination isn't the best. Such a lovely surprise bday. 

The martini and chocolate cake didn't do me any good so the rest of the night will be chill. Time to enjoy the last of this fabulous hotel before we go back to $3 a night hostels. What a fantastic bday!!


Pics check it: https://m.flickr.com/#/photos/cleatus_cobb/

items.title: Annapurna done! Happy early bday to me! 12/16
items.body:
We woke up at 5 in an attempt to find a flight out of here. There's no one up. We walk w our headlamps looking for the airport. We find the ticket office after wandering for 30 min. It's almost 6 and nothin is open and we are sitting in the freezing cold w all our shit. The chances of this happening aren't good. After 15 min or so, we hear movement inside. A dude opens the door. Flights for Pokhara? Yes. Yes!! Holy shit we are going to get out of here!!

We pay the $230 and walk to the airport. Flying out of a secondary airport in a 3rd world country is interesting. The waiting room was outside. I'm tired of being cold. There is one flight in and one out each day. They are first thing in the morning before the wind picks up. The flight in was late but who cares, we aren't on a 20 hour bus ride of hell. They "check" our bags since there are no X-rays. There's no checking, they open one thing in our bags and ask if we have any lighters. Nope? We are all good. 

We airplane lands and we rush to board, all wanting a good seat. This plane is 3 seats wide and maybe 8 back. We both get a window seat on the left side to see the mountains. I look at Andy w love in case this is the last time I see him. He smiles, I know he's nervous too as he just mentioned "these are the planes that crash all the time". Yeah thanks I know. What could go wrong flying past the Annapurna mountains in a small plane in a 3rd world country?!

The flight was calm and amazingly beautiful! We saw the Annapurna range on our left as we flew above the fog (apparently we've been hiking above the fog too). Not only did we make it to Pokhara in 20 min, the scenery of the flight was worth the cost. So happy to be here!

We aimed for the Lake District. It was close to the airport so we walked and looked for a hotel. On the way we grabbed some oranges, samosas, and honey deep fried. How do you deep fry honey and make it taste as amazing as it sounds?! 

We stopped at the fabulous Glacier Lake Hotel w an amazing lake view. The manager showed us the penthouse first (they are 20% of capacity and were expecting 50%). The room is on the 8th floor, by itself, jacuzzi, and it's own terrace over looking the lake?! Hell yeah! It's my bday!! When we checked in they gave us a watermelon drink then a real latte. A real latte! Did I mention we have the whole top floor?!

We took our first real shower in 2 weeks and left a huge dirt ring in the tub. Eww. We are mending our wounds, blisters, losing a toenail... We slowly made out way down to breakfast at 10:30, already feeling like we've had a full day. Andy had a mushroom omelette and a rösti, I had french toast to continue my honey kick. We also had a banana and one pineapple lassi. Freaking delish. I spent the next couple hours reading in the swing on our terrace enjoying the warm sun. Im thinking we need to spend another day here because it doesn't look like we are going to get out much today. 



We finally ventured out into civilization and made a couple purchases. I'm not a great negotiator but I think I've found the best method. I do a crappy job negotiating, Andy says sorry, we only have this much and shows the wallet. We end up w little debate and get a good deal. 

We walked around waiting for happy hour and we ran into a bunch of people we were on the circuit with. They were over it just like we were but they took the bus down. Glad we missed that. Paul said it was worse than the Death Road in Bolivia. They tried not to be scared unless the locals made an "oooh" sound. We hit up a bar by the lake and watched the sunset and shared hiking stories. Good times.

items.title: Down the mountain we go 12/15 Day13
items.body:
We have no destination we must reach so we took it easy this am. Breakfast consisted of potato omelette for Andy, good ol Tibetan Bread w honey and boiled eggs for me. 

We took off at 9:30 and headed for Kagbeni. We headed down again, not like yesterday, but still some switchbacks. The weather was nice, sun out w a slight breeze. We hit Kagbeni at 1. It was a very cool town, reminded us of Fez. We would have liked to stay there, we saw Chance and the Aussie, but we wanted to push on. 

The next 2 hours were intense through the wind tunnel. It was flat, along the river bed, but the wind was intense w dust devils, and walking on river bed stones sucks ass. We hit Jomsom at 3:30, its a crappy town and we are tired. It's time for some warmth and animals (Chitwan)! Tomorrow we'll try to hit up Pokhara if we can. Schools have shut down here due to the cold!

The dude at the bus ticket counter told me they were sold out. Then I said I'll buy tickets for the day after. How much? I don't know. WTF. Are you being difficult because I'm female or because we have a communication problem. Turns out the guys in our hostel are trying to get off the mountain too. We have to catch the bus to Ghasa and take other buses off the mountain. We have no cash and the dude said all the ATMs were closed and he got the last $75 out of the open one. Umm. The other dude said it took his friend the entire day of transferring buses and she reached Pokhara at midnight. That blows. Or, the flights to Pokhara are sounding pretty good right now. We have time, $200+ might offset the hassle...

The room we had dinner in was so cold, they didn't turn on the heater. I had the Dal Bhat and Andy had fried chicken. Lomsom sucks (at least in the off season), we are tired of being cold, and I think we need a change of scenery. We go up to the room and Andy says, we are going for the flight tomorrow. Yes! Hopefully the travel gods will be in our favor.

items.title: Thorang La Pass F yeah 17.8k!! 12/14 Day 12
items.body:
Up before the alarm because of the loud ass kids. No worries, I slept like shit from a major headache and wanted to get the day started. No breakfast, that would just allow my body to get cold. We packed and got on our way by 6:30. 

I know I've been saying it cold everyday, but it's really fucking cold. I wish I knew the temperature but it must have been -20 w the slight breeze. Andy's eyelashes froze and he an icicle off of his headlamp. My gloves froze and then after a slight panic attack, Andy warmed my hands against his body and I put on the parka. I'm always reminded how much he takes care of me when we travel. I wouldn't do this stuff w just anyone! I thought we were going to kill it up to the pass since we've been doing so well. That 2k ft to the pass was fucking hard! I mean real hard. We took small steps and then had to break since the oxygen was so low. We climbed for ~2 hours and hit the pass! I was so excited a little tear came to my eye- or maybe it was due to almost body failure. This is really the hardest physical thing I've done in my life. 

At top we took some pics, awed at the beauty of the day and mountains, and got excited to go down. Andy got a pic w his work launch badge and a Goodpeople Tshirt. We didn't want to stay too long up there since it was 17.5k high and that's not good for a body. Stoked to go down! I mean the hardest part was behind us right? Hell no. 



The next 3 hours of going down was over ice, steep slopes w rocks that make you slip, and 3 hours is a long time to trek on that shit. The view on this side was very different. It was like we were walking on a glacier on one side, rocks on the other. It didn't feel like we were moving much. We powered through and got to Muktinath. 

Unfortunately the kids were trekking w us. We decided to bypass the Bob Marley hotel because that's where they were staying (sorry Bob, I'm sure you would have done the same w people who were so not down). We opted for The Path of Dreams hotel. We took our first shower in 10 days! Thank you Patagonia sports bra for becoming one w my body, but I need to trade you out. It was a cold not nice shower but I'll take it. We ran into the guy who was sick and Andy gave him magic pills. The dude was so grateful! He said thank you over and over. Those pills were the reason the dude got over the hill. Very cool. 
 
Sitting in the sunroom makes everything OK, or maybe it's the beer we are having to celebrate. Either way, we made it, we are warm and enjoying our accomplishment. We have no plans for what the next several days lay ahead of us. I think a mountain bike ride is in our future, or maybe we'll hit up some animals in Chitwan. Dinner consisted of pizza and yak burger. The burger wasn't bad, there was curry in it. First time having meat in about 2 weeks!
https://m.flickr.com/#/photos/cleatus_cobb/ 
26k steps, 13 miles

items.title: Thorang Base Camp 16k 12/13 Day 11
items.body:
Not sure what happened last night but some dude started screaming at 11 and flash lights were going crazy. It was probably the roxi. 
It was cold this am!! The dude wipes froze on me and the toilet water was frozen solid.  Our sleeping bags are the best thing we've ever brought. We are so warm it's hard to get out. We got a huge breakfast of museli, potatoes, boiled eggs, Tibetan Bread w honey and tea (I ate most of it). We were going to get a late start but the sun wasn't hitting us yet and I was getting really cold. We started at 8 and reached Thorang Phedi in less than 2 hours. It wasn't too intense except for the 10 switchbacks we had to clim because we followed the porter instead of the route. 

We stopped for some masala tea and continued on to high camp. It took us an hour of switchbacks to make it to High Camp but we did it! We climbed 2133 ft to 16k today and we feel good. Gotta love those side trips we took! We are the only ones on the mountain again. I guess the people we were traveling w made it over this am. The sun is shinning, the sky is blue, and we can see the tops of several snow covered Annapurna. So far making it to High Camp was totally worth it! 

Just as we were settling down to enjoy the fire, 12 early 20somethings barged in and ruined the vibe. They were the worst. I have a hard time imagining I was that bad but maybe I was. We ate our 2nd rösti of the day w yak cheese and veg fried noodles plus warm rice pudding then we fled for our room. Kids say the dumbest shit, and they are loud. Might as well get to bed early since tomorrow is a big day!!

items.title: Climbing for 4 hrs plus a rest day! 12/12 Day 10
items.body:
Up at our normal time and a quick breakfast of apples and muesli w warm sugar yak milk and Andy had a veg omelette. I'm all about the more calories for my buck. We were on the trail before 8 since we weren't interested in chatting up the other folks in the hotel- lets just say they all showered last night. I don't have anything against it, but we are in the Himalaya dammit, the locals don't take warm showers. I don't think we've showered in 10 days? Well not completely unclean. Those Burts Bees peach and willow bark wipes have done my face and important parts wonders. I wouldn't use them at home since it's wasteful, out here it's critical. I wish I could use them on my socks. 

Anyways, we quickly made it to Yak Kharka in under 3 hours (yay porter!) where we saw the Aussie kids from Tilicho Lake w their friend who's had diarrhea for 6 days. The kid doesn't want to take any pills but can't walk more than 40 min without having to take a poop. Andy, being the caring guy that he is, gave the friends 4 pills for the guy's stomach issues. They were annoyed the guy wouldn't take anything, so maybe w these magic stop pooping pills will do the trick since they want to summit tomorrow. That guy is too dehydrated to summit, bad idea. 

We push on to Letdar which is at 14k with no problems. All the acclimation hikes we did seem to be paying off. We reached the hotel before noon and busted out the yak cheese and Ritz (you read that right!) and it was the most delicious thing I've ever eaten. We should have bought more than our $2 worth of cheese. 

We spent the rest of the afternoon in the sunroom reading and relaxing. So happy to have a rest day after hiking for 4 hours. We petted the kitty. She was a little grey thing w beautiful greenish blue eyes. She was a total lover digging the face rubs until she was over it and tried to swat Andy. No more petting. Once that sun goes down its going to be cold!! The wind picks up in the afternoon, that's why we hike early as possible. Tomorrow should be a good day too, planning on reaching high camp before the pass!! I think we'll get a large thermos of tea before bed so we have something warm to wake up to (a great idea from another Aussie friend). We are the only travelers in this little village. Time to enjoy some alone time before we get back to crazy.

items.title: Prepping for the summit 12/11 Day 9
items.body:
We had to backtrack back to Manang today to get our heavy shit. I think Andy now understands the beautiful feeling of not carrying a heavy load because he's not discounting my porter comments. We set off after 8 w the crew after a breakfast of Tibetan Bread and honey. Man was it good. 

It was really cold this am, I was pacing waiting for people and my toes went numb. It was probably negative last night but we were still warm in our bags! Too warm actually. Not a bad problem to have at this altitude. 

We passed the scary landslide area w no issues. Going up the scree is much easier than going down. We took the lower path by accident and ended up crossing the ravine over the icy rocks. Andy went first and crushed some of the ice for everyone so we could step on rocks not ice, Paul called him a machine. The machine is back! Although we had to hike back up the hill, we passed the terrifying switchbacks against the cliff that I was dreading. 

A short break, the crew stopped for lunch before heading for Yak Kharka and we broke off for Manang. Walking along the ridge, an eagle hovered over us no more than 10 ft. It was huge! Probably had a wingspan of 7 ft and the body probably sat 3 ft tall. It could have done some damage to us and we were a bit nervous as it hovered above us for 10 seconds. Amazing!  We reached the town after 1 and the wind was howling. After 5 hours of hiking I wasn't really down for 4 more so we called it a day. 

The rest of the day we spent prepping for the pass, getting a porter (yay!), and eating and relaxing. I got some of the most fantastic apple crisp and read a bit. It's going to snow tonight. It's gnarly out there! I hope it warms up a bit for the pass or I'm hiking in my big puffy jacket. 
I now understand I won't have a rest day. I just want to get over this pass. 
24k steps, 11 miles

items.title: Lake Tilicho at 16k ft 12/10 Day 8
items.body:
No rush today since we were only going up the mountain and back but we got up at the normal time anyway. It snowed last night. It actually woke us up and it sounded like hail. Snow isn't what we need, it could make the path back to Manang impossible. It was just a light dusting. Breakfast consisted of doughy apple pancakes and two eggs each and shit coffee. Time to stick to tea. 

We headed up at 8 w the crew. The walk up wasn't too bad, it was pretty gradual except for 15 or so switchbacks. A couple landslide areas, but I was numb from the intense scree yesterday so they weren't a big deal. There was a lot of ice at the top which slowed our hike. It took us 3.5 hours to reach the lake at 16k ft which was 2.8k up from the lodge. 

The lake was beautiful and blue. The skies were clear, and we were lucky to see some glaciers moaning and cracking and a small landslide into the lake. It was a bit windy but the closed hut blocked the wind. I was surprised how good we felt at the top. We took the sun and scenery in for 30 min. Only places this hard to get to are this beautiful. I'm so glad we had enough time for this side trek. 

The hike down was pretty easy and sun was hitting us the whole way. We reached the lodge at 2 and finally had some time to relax. The lodge was so hot from the sun beating in, just what we needed. Then we are some veg spring rolls and Tibetan Bread which is fried dough for an appetizer. Since they take forever w food, and Andy finally wanted to eat (yay!), we ordered fried noodles w egg and fried potatoes to get our carbs on. Less people around the fire tonight. We saw the 3 Indian girls and the hippie walk in. They only have jean jackets on and look so cold. I'm trying to stay away until 7. We'll see how far we press on tomorrow. Back to Manang and maybe Yak Kharka.

items.title: I failed my duty of being the voice of reason 12/9 Day 7
items.body:
We didn't know what we were going to do when we woke up. Andy wanted to do Tilicho Lake w the others, I was up for it but didn't want to bring the heavy ass bags. Over a breakfast of museli, we decided to leave a bag here and head out w the group of 4 Australians, a German, and another American. We packed super light with only the necessities,  we'll be wearing the same clothes for a few days. We were almost out of cash, luckily Andy found a place to exchange our USD. I'm not sure what we would have done, we still have many days on the mountain. 

We started at 8:30. It was an easy hike to Khangsar. It was supposed to take 3 hours, it took 1.5. We took a lot of breaks enjoying the sun along the way. We stopped for lunch at Siri Kharka. The weather was perfect, sunny and blue skies. 

After a couple hours in, it was time for the infamous landslide area. This shit was legit and terrifying. I should have said no fucking way (voice of reason part), but we went. The first landslide part had a herd of mused deer (blue sheep/ look like rams). We stopped and let the rocks fall in front of our path. If we took one misstep, we would have fallen to our death below. I couldn't look down, just where I needed to step. Some parts you had to slide down the path and watch the mountain fall away. I went first and Andy followed. The switchbacks got me. I had to slide down and carefully turn. At one point a guy we were with had a leg cramp and we had to pass him. He had multiple cramps and Andy had to go back for him at one point. It was the most intense path I've ever been on and it took over an hour. 

We made it to Tilicho Base Camp lodge at 3:30. The lodge is lovely w windows all around with a view of the mountains and glaciers around us. Reaching the lodge made the hike worth it- we went up another 1600 ft today to 14k. The lodge owners started the fire at 5 and everyone quickly surrounded it. It put out so much warmth and the wind was kickin outside. For dinner we had mushroom soup w Ritz and fried noodles. So damn good.  Let's see how well we sleep at this altitude and with the wind howling. The stars are our but half the sky is covered by a big cloud.  Tomorrow is going to be intense heading up to Tilicho Lake.

items.title: Kicking ass and acclimating at Ice Lake 12/8 Day 6
items.body:
We took our time today, had lunch at 7:30 of veg omlettes and hit up the bakery downstairs for a chocolate croissant and cinnamon roll- they were massive. We saved most of the goods for the hike. 

We started on our journey at 9:30. Crossed the road in Bhraga, up toward one of the bigger monasteries we've seen, traversed the hail and started the switchbacks up the mountain. Andy is still pretty sick but he's a beast so we decided to climb the mountain. We took our time, slow and steady, planning for how we would take the overpass. We didn't have our bags on today and it was amazing! It felt so good it made me sad to think about how fucking heavy our bags are. 

Walking up the mountain is kinda like meditating, all you can do is watch where you step and breathe w your steps. It was very peaceful, we were walking at such a pace we weren't losing our breathe. We made good time though. We hit the lookout point in 1.5 hours and it was supposed to take 2. We would pause every now and then to take in the view. We could see Annapurna 2, 3, and 4. We were so high, we hiked up 4K ft. The town and valley was so small from our viewpoint. The trail was full of false peaks- we kept thinking we were there and we weren't. 

We passed a heard of Rams w their huge curved antlers. They were running across the mountain trying to get away from us. A condor flew just above our head, probably thinkng we were dead. The sun was hitting us all day, we sat for a bit on a pasture to take in the view and eat our baked good that were now warm from the sun. We decided to go up one more section, if the lake wasn't there then f it. Luckily it was a flat walk and we finally made it to Ice Lake at 1592 ft. The lake itself was ok, but there was a herd of yaks drinking from it. The yaks, the lake, the view of the Himalaya, it was a other National Geographic moment. We didn't stay long at the top, Andy thought my lips were turning blue and I had a headache (since I was still hungry I wasn't worried about altitude sickness). 

We made it to the top in 4.5 hours w our breaks, we made it down the mountain in less than 2. Going down is really hard, it's hard on the quads and it's hard not slipping on the lose rocks. Plus we were tired. We grabbed our bags from the New Yak and headed for Manang. Sooo tired, it was cold, and I was very hungry. The walk was supposed to be 30 min, more like 45, but when you are that tired, 15 min is a huge diff.  We grabbed a room in the same place as the rest of the travelers we met yesterday. First priority is the change and get food. We had ginger lemon honey tea, soup, spring rolls, and French fries. I'm still hungry. Andy thinks I'm eating a lot. This is nothing for all the calories we are burning. I'm a machine and I need energy dammit! Tomorrow we are either taking a rest day or hiking for ~8 hours to start the Tilicho Lake hike. If we go we can go w friends, I'm needing a rest day. We'll see. I'm really hating my bag weight. Other people have a small tiny bag w them. I'm so jealous. I'm also now ok w not taking a shower until we end our trek (it's too cold) and brushing my teeth once a day. My hair braids are turning into dreads.   
30k steps, 15 miles, 4K ft

items.title: Best day ever (so far) 12/7 Day 5
items.body:
Up at 6 and had breakfast w our new Croatian friends. I tried the local porridge which wasn't so good. Luckily Andy didn't eat much of his muesli so I killed it. We took off before the Croatians since our bags are much heavier and we figured they would catch up (they didn't). It was cold, but it wasn't for too long until we hit the sun. A nice flatish walk and then we started the uphill. And uphill we did for 1300 ft, straight up w our heavy ass bags. We did well, slow and steady. We made it up in 2 hours. At the top we took in the view of Annapurna 2 w some Himalyan apples and mushroom noodle soup and lemon ginger tea. Just what we needed. 

After an hour of not seeing our friends, it was time to head for Bhraga. All the villages in this area are made out of stone. With the flags flying, it's like Game of Thrones. We walked along the ridge for a couple hours. The views from the top of the mountain range was unbelievable. We could even see the snow topped bowl rock we passed yesterday. The sun was shining and there was a slight breeze. Perfect for hiking. Words can't express the beauty. It's like National Geographic. We passed more herders and their yaks. We saw 10 or more condors flying high and circling us. Those suckers were big. We hit the next village and headed down. We opted for the road instead of the path since it was more direct and we had several more hours. Even when we intercepted it we co to used on the dusty road. What a good choice it was. 

Around the bend we hit a small town and saw our goal off in the distance. We were hurtin and wanted to be done asap. Luckily Bhraga was just around another bend. It was almost 4 when we arrived. Another loooong hiking day. The town was smaller than I expected. I checked out Hotel Buddha and Andy checked out New Yak Hotel. I didn't want to stay at New Yak because it's a pun, but there were other travelers there. It ended it being the place to be! The in had a little cat and we welcomed her into our room. She was the sweetest. She jumped onto our sleeping bags and purred and snuggled w us.  In the restaurant they got the fire going and we sat 20 travelers around it. There were people from Canada, China, Australia, UK, Chile, and a dude from FL. He had been traveling fo a while and has hardly met any Americans. He passed the Croatians on the way in who told us we were here. He barges in the room and says "are you the Americans!?". He just came from India and we got a lot of good travel tip from him for our next journey. For dinner we had garlic noodle soup, a huge veggie burger (it was like a stuffing patty- so good), and a pizza which was actually really good and legit. It's almost 9 and way past our bedtime. I'm hoping tomorrow will be an easy day but I doubt it. Andy is sick but refusing to slow down. He was a beast today when he should be sleeping. 
30k steps, 16 miles

items.title: Pressing on into pine tree forests 12/6 Day 4
items.body:
Up at 6 and breakfast at 7 in the tiny room they call a restaurant. This time we had museli w apples and and egg. Last night a horse nayed right by our window, pretty freaky when you are sleeping. Andy is sick, he caught my cold. Poor guy. 

The hike started very nice, flat for as flat can be around here. We followed some schools children and a dog to Thanchowk. It was pretty chilly without having sun on us. This side of the mountain does that much sun in the winter. We stopped in Koto for some masala tea and the hiker check point. The children got us again w their namastes. I think the only English words they know are chocolate and some like biscuit or biscotti. Oh no you don't, no more sweets from us (plus it's frowned upon). Andy's cold was hitting him hard. It was nice to soak up a little sun, especially since last night was so foggy and damp. 

We made great time to Chame. We set high goals for reaching Upper Pisang so I pushed for us to use the road instead of the trail. The trail is the scenic route, not the fast way. Plus, these fucking maps are terrible. They are just fucking wrong so it's hard to make the right call on where to go. It's not that you'll get lost, you just might take longer than expected. Walking through the pine forests was lovely. So peaceful plus the smell of pine always makes me smile. 

We stopped in Bhratang for lunch. We learned from the last couple days that Beth needs to eat so she doesn't have a breakdown (I cried a bit at the end of our uphill hike yesterday). Plus this place is known for their apples, it's a whole valley of orchards. We have an apple pancake and garlic noodle soup. So good. Although it was already 2, we decided to make the push for our destination. One of the mountains when hiking looked so odd. It was like one piece of rock w some layers falling away. It was so huge, it took up the entire side of a valley, and it was in a bowl shape. The shape of it made us feel very small. We made good time, it took us 2.5 hours to get to Upper Pisang instead of the 4 expected. Food does wonders!

We were hiking on the high trial to UP, then I noticed Lower Pisang along the road, just beneath UP. It sounds logical, but the fucking maps make it look like UP is closer. So your telling me I didn't have to hike up a hill? Wtf. We find a great hotel (the town apparently doesn't have wifi) and we meet other foreigners! I was starting to think we were the only people on the mountain. They are very nice and from Croatia, here to cross the pass in just 8 days. We sit by the fire and chat. We shared a large thermos of lemon ginger honey tea and we eat a veg spring roll, veg momos, and mushroom soup for dinner. I could eat more but I'll save it for breakfast. I love that you tell themwhat time you want breakfast and what to eat and it's all ready. Today was intense. 38k steps, 19 miles. I really want a rest day.

items.title: The bee that almost killed me 12/5 Day 3
items.body:
Up at 6 again after 11 hours of fantastic sleep. Breakfast consisted of musli and two hard boiled eggs each. Between last nights dinner, breakfast and our room the bill was $20 (rooms are $3). We left the valley on a nice flattish walk. As we walk down to the river, we walked through hundreds of fucking huge bees. These bastards are 2-3x US standards. I didn't panic until one got near my face. Then I tried to run only to notice it was fucking stuck in my braid. Andy is yelling "stand still"! I try to compose myself enough to stop and I brace for the stinger. Andy gets it out of my hair and I notice the cliff I almost threw myself down trying to escape it. That was a bit of a traumatic experience for the morning. Thank god the rest of them just sat there instead of swarming. Then I'm sure I'd be over the cliff, or running down the hill into the river. They are seriously fucking huge. 

We bypass some of the trail for the road and make great time to Dharapani. We took a quick break and watched little lambs in the yard. They were so new, he had it's umbilical cord still attached. They jumped up on the rock fence where we were sitting. One licked Andy's shirt and once licked my arms for salt. So cute! It's not an issue passing the 3 jeeps on the road. The road was a bit sketchy, walking under huge boulders. Some parts had boulders in the road likely from the earthquake. The other rocks in the mountain had crevices, looking like they were waiting to be shook loose.  On the other side of the valley we could see where a huge boulder, like 50 ft in diameter, had fallen from the side of the mountain and landed in the river.   We passed a herd of yaks w red ornaments in their ears. Don't look at them in the eye and hopefully they won't push you off the road. The road was steep to Bagarchap but nothing compared to the stairs we took up the mountain to get to Timang. It must have been 2k ft of nothing but stairs. We finally saw an Annapuna (4 I believe)! The snow covered mountains tops are beautiful in the sun. Then when we were close to the top, we had to climb using tree roots to get to the top. We were dirty, tired, and we hadn't eaten anything since 7am, it was 2. 

We made it to Timang, got a lovely room looking at the mountains. For linnder we had ginger lemon honey tea, garlic & mushroom noodle soup, and we each had a veg & egg spring roll made from scratch. The tea was the most delicious, all the food was really. We sat in the tiny room watching the lady make all our food while the fog rolled in. Then towns men then came in and she fed them as well. It looked like it was a potato dish w fresh tortillas. Everything is from scratch here and delish. I feel bad for ordering momos yesterday because they take so long. Maybe we'll do spring rolls from here on out- no meat (I don't need a chicken to die in front of me at the moment). 

Now it's 3:30 so we are in our sleeping bags reading and relaxing. No wifi here. It's cold. This might be when I stop showering. I'm nervous what the rest of the hike will bring. The views are amazing. It's definitely a workout. 
25k steps, 12 miles, 120 floors

items.title: Holy shit that was a lot of up 12/4 Day 2
items.body:
Whomever said this hike was moderately difficult I want to bitch slap them. Today was really hard. 

Up at 5 due to a large thud in the ceiling. No matter, plenty of sleep. We had musli for breakfast w warm sweet milk and hard boiled eggs. Lots of food for our journey. We started before 8 again. The air was crisp and perfect for hiking. A little dog from the village w a bell on its collar followed us out of town. I was worried because he followed us fo a while, until we reached the next village no the dog faced the village dog. The small one following us tried to play w the other dog, then I heard a squeal. Hopefully it didn't end too poorly.  We took the road for a bit and saw our first pair of foreigners and they had a porter. I knew it wouldn't be busy, but we are really the only ones in these villages. I saw the red and white marker taking us off the road, which went up. We grabbed some marsala tea about an hour in a the top of the hill in Jagat. Little did we know what we had ahead. Back down a bit and then up to Chamje. 

After Chamje we crossed an Indiana Jones-like bridge. First I went to the middle, looking down only to where I'm stepping, not to the death that lays below. When Andy came to join me, he was walking w too much of a bounce in his step and I didn't care for that. We noticed some large dents in the bridge from previously fallen boulders. No worry, how unsafe can a bridge be in the mountains in a a third world country?

As we started up the hill, there was a lot of movement next to us. Andy saw a fucking cobra slithering away, about 2 inches in diameter. Well we knew they were here. I'm glad he's trailblazing. Next we came across a flock of goats as we started up the hill. There were probably over 100 old and babies. We tried to move to the side of the trail, they were coming down fast and there was a lot of them. Andy was rammed a couple times. 

Walking up the mountain, we had a great view of the gnarly "road" on the other side, chiseled out of the side of the mountain. Probably as scary as the death road in Bolivia. Jeeps were honking in parts, not sure why, it's not like anyone was getting over or backing up. The scenery is amazing. There are odd palm trees on the ridge at the top of the mountain. We hike under large beautiful rhododendron trees and bamboo. 

Next we walked up, a fucking lot. Once we thought we were at the top, we walked down and saw the huge mountain we had to walk up. It was nuts and we were tired. We have to be getting close right? We reached the top and hit the gateway into Tal at 1:30. We were so happy! The valley widened and there was a rushing river and a sandy beach glistening in the sun. We walked through town and Andy found us a lovely hotel on the edge of town called Paraside next to the waterfall. Wifi and comfy beds check! 

We dropped out shit and went outside to enjoy the last of the sunshine. We laid down our sleeping mats in the grass for a little yoga. I was starving. All the menus are the same up here and they say they have everything. I really want pizza but I'm not sure I can trust them. We stuck w momo's, cheese and veg/potato, along w a real ginger tea and local beer that tasted like sour beer. The food was delish. I wanted more. It's only 3:30. We read our books and read about more fucking shootings back home. 5:30 rolls around and the dude offers us the menu. Andy declines. Really?! I need to eat! I'm going to need all the energy I can get for tomorrow. Is it time for bed yet? The sun is down, the wind is blowing, and it's cold! Can't wait for my sleeping bag!!
25k steps, 12+ miles, 2k feet net gain, lots of up and down.

items.title: Finally nature! 12/3 Day 1
items.body:
Up at 6 and enjoying the sounds of the water rushing near us. We slept well in our sleeping bags, well I did. Andy had to get his in the middle of the night because he passed out w all his clothes on. We took our time getting ready. The young girl didn't understand me asking for breakfast so we packed up and headed out before 8. The trail was the road at this point, however there are no cars. We hiked up and up and up. The scenery was beautiful. We passed villages covered in rhododendrons and hibiscus. Villagers were extracting oats from the stalked. The children are adorable! They love saying "namaste" as we pass. One little girl got me w a namaste and wanted some of my Pringles she saw on the outside of my bag (I put them there in case of emergency). The hillsides were covered in rice fields. Baby goats and chickens in th villages. This is what we've been waiting for! 

We stopped at the top of the hill at Bahundanda for some Nepali tea and rested under Banyan tree. It was after 10 and we pushed on. Back down the hill undoing all the uphill work we put in. We made it to Ghermu Phant and I needed to eat. We ate some veg fried rice (again) and veg curry rice w egg (light on the curry- not by choice), wrapped it up w Nepali tea. Food was just what we needed to reenergize us. Two little boys walked by and hooked us w some namastes then asked for chocolate. Andy couldn't resist so we got out one of our little Snickers and shared it w them. 

The last leg was down the hill to Syange by the river and waterfall. We crossed a long shifty bridge that some goat hearders were trying to push their heard across. The goats weren't having it so the guys were picking them up and shoving them. We got a room. It's after 2.  Time for some beer and wifi! We passed out at 8 after our dinner of momo's, worth the 2 hour wait.
We hiked for ~5 hours today, 6.7 miles, 1300 feet up net (several ups and down). https://www.flickr.com/photos/cleatus_cobb/

items.title: Travel day, a tiring one 12/2
items.body:
Up at 4:30 this am and one last coffee on the rooftop before heading to the bus stop at 7. Th ride was uneventful, we watched the countryside pass by, happy to be out of the city. After several pit stops and 3 samosas, we were on our way w lots of oranges, a small Snickers, Pringles, and a pomelo. We knew we were getting closer to Dumre, we saw a couple shops that had that as the city as we passed by. Andy quickly ran to the driver who stopped the bus and dropped us off. Good thing we were paying attention! We'd be in Pokhara. 

We walked back to Dumre and Andy found a local bus to take us to Bessishara. He had to take an emergency bathroom break, he ran into a local stor and asked to the dude to use his restroom. It had no lights so Andy had to use his phone to see the hole in the ground. Worst bathroom ever he says. That's a strong statement. 

I love elected us to sit on top of the bus. Why not? Can't do that shit in the US. The rack on the top was metal bars welded together. It hurt to sit on them, and hurt to have the small of your back against it. There wasn't much room so Andy sat on the back w nothing between him and the ground in case there was a sudden movement. About half hour in the dude made us get in the bus due to police. Thank god, my ass was killing me, plus the rest of the ride was really bumpy. 

When we got to Bessishara we decided to take one last bus to Ngadi. Bessishara was a small city w too many people and we wanted to save some time for the tail end of the trip. Good thing. We bypassed all the construction the Chinese are doing for the hydroelectric dam. It would not have been nice to walk past. The ride was pretty scary. We were very  close to the cliff, so close I had to look away. Andy watched the road fall away over the ravine. Then the bus swayed back and forth, feeling like it was possible that we were going over. I prefer to look away and not see my fate. It's times like this that I miss US safety standards. 

The bus was full of people and then I got a huge gas pain in my stomach. It was so painful going over the rocks and ditches in the "road". They were blasting music and I wanted to die. An hour later we made it, right before sunset, and I finally felt better. Our room is very basic and we'll sleep in our bags. We were the only ones here so they made dinner especially for us. A beer, ginger tea, mushroom soup, and two veg and egg rice. No meat for Andy today! I haven't been able to eat much meat on this trip. In fact I might go all veg. Also, there are huge spiders and Cobras here. There are signs to watch where you shit. Nice.

items.title: A day w few plans turned out to be amazing 12/1
items.body:
Awake at 3, I guess we really didn't conquer jet lag after all. Relaxed until 6 then it was coffee time on the rooftop to watch the city come alive (and see dog fights). We headed for Helenas for breakfast, 8 floors up to the highest rooftop restaurant. The sun was shining and there was a slight breeze. I had the double croissant breakfast (don't judge) and Andy stayed true to the local cuisine and had the Aloo Parathna. 

We broke out the Annapurna map and a dude came over and asked about if we were going to hike. Turns out Evan (from Portland by way of Ohio) has been to Nepal 4 times and Annapurna twice. He gave us great advice and made us feel very comfortable hiking it alone. Just what we needed! Now we have a couple side hikes planned and the DL on where to stay. Unfortunately for me Evan got Andy stoked about using the bivies so I may have that in my future. Evan is trying to start microlending in Nepal and help out some kids get to college along the way. 

We headed out to pick up our Tibet visas before 11. The weather was cooler than previous days which was so nice. Then we start walking and warm up. I have no idea how the Nepalese are wearing heavy winter jackets when it's 70 out. I guess this is their winter. We got out Tibet visas (yay!) and stopped by a travel agency to see if we could get the flight to Tibet cheaper than online- nope. I guess $675 each round trip is the best we can do (for an hour flight WTF!). No stamp on our passports for Tibet, only the entry/exit papers. 

Next we walk an hour or so to the Sree Pashupatinath Temple and paid our foreigner fee of 1000 Rupees (~$10). Andy tried to walk in the Hindu nationalists only temple but was turned away. We ran into a lady from the Netherlands (a practicing Buddist) who just signed up for the guide and offered for us to join. I was hesitant, Andy said yes, so we went. After a quick tour of the temple from the outside, we went down to the river. This isn't any river, this is a holy river. Just as we walked up, a family was prepping their beloved to be cremated. We were just 20 feet away and saw the three sons change the corpse's clothes from white to orange, walk around the bed that was fully covered in orange carnations 3 times, then the eldest son placed a flame in the corpse's mouth to start the cremation. We saw the body, the head, and it all catch on fire right in front of us. It was pretty intense for me, not so much for everyone else who's seen it many times. After the body burns for 3 hours for males, 4 for females (because females have "a spine that takes longer to burn", the ashes are placed in the river. Once the body covered in wood and hay was fully ablaze, we headed for the cave while quickly walking rough the black smoke. 

Between that, the garbage on fire, and walking to the temple in the smog, I was wasn't feeling well. We walked to the top of the hill that had a great view of the temple, hospice building, and another buidling that's open to the poor and sick of 60 and older (Mother Teresa lived there for a bit). We passed some Holy Men and the woman we were w really wanted her pic taken w them. No thanks I said. She said it was an amazing experience. Ok fine then. I saw next to one and he took his dreads down and draped the over me. They surprisingly didn't smell. He blessed me and then it was Andy's turn. Our littl tour group drank some Nepalses tea (black tea w milk and cinnamon), getting to know our new friend and guide a little better. 

Next we headed out for Boudhanath Stupa Temple. This is a large dome temple that lost the top during the earthquake, they were building "stairs" on the roof to start the reconstruction. We walked around clockwise and toured the town. It was 3 and time for food. We stopped at a restaurant that advertised a ton of food, but only had momo's which was cool because that's all we wanted. The wifi password was "nofoodnogas" so they were obviously feeling the effects of the India blockade. I had the potato and cheese momo's and Andy had to beef "buff" ones. Not quite perogies but delish. 

Headed back to Thamel, I was tired and the fumes were killing me so we took a taxi back during rush hour. Our last stop was to drop off the school supplies. The tracking agency was open. The guy responsible for the connection to packforapurpose.com sat us down and asked us about ourselves as Andy showed them the prints and school supplies we brought. The people were stoked and we felt awesome knowing it would go to use for a middle grade school. 

It's been another long day. It was great, and I'm happy to exit this city tomorrow as we head out to start Annapurna- after a 6 hour bus ride for $12. 
Walked 24k steps; 13 miles; 21 floors

items.title: We made it! Get me a beer 11/29
items.body:
We finally reached the gate for Kathmandu at 3 AM. Our flight was supposed to leave around 7 but it was scheduled for 8:45 so I took a nap sitting up on the chairs. I'm getting good at this. 
A short easy flight and we finally made it! We paid the $40 each Nepal visa and grabbed a cab for the Avalon hostel. 

The hostel is in Thamel off the main road so it's a little quieter. It's on the 2nd floor w great views of the city to the West, not so good for earthquakes. We can see kids playing and women cleaning, not sure what the men are doing. Not bad for $12/night, we even have our own bathroom. Andy is excited for the twin beds since I won't be kicking him tonight. Can't wait to see how much places outside the city cost. 

It's noon so we rest for a moment then head out to explore the city a bit. We find the main shopping area in Thamel, get some water, a scarf for all this smog, and a map of Annapurna. We finally grab some beers and food at a rooftop Thai restaurant. I order the soup as foreigner medium spicy and it's still too hot for me.   We relax and feel whats it's like on the first real day of our vaca. Nepal resembles India more than I expected. I'm sure that will change as we get out of the city. 


We head back for the room and decide to take a nap at 3. I don't think that's a good idea. I bet we end up sleeping the rest of the night. Yep, we do.

items.title: I'm gonna need some fresh air 11/30
items.body:
We slept for 13 hours, woke up at 4am and felt like champs. Andy needed some coffee so he went downstairs for hot water. He returns w/ a tea set and we head to the rooftop w our Counter Culture coffee and grind some of our own (see what you've created Anthony/Kristina?). The smell of fireplace is strong w/in our room. The smell of the orange carnations is strong everywhere at this time of day. 
We took a walk at 7 waiting for the hostel dude to print our Tibet permits and hoping to find food to no avail. Although people are up and at em by 6, no stores until 8 or 9. We give up on the prints and head to the China Embassy to get our Tibet visa after stopping for breakfast. Breakfast was a huge meal of Indian food and an omelette (it was hard to eat after I pulled the hair from it but dammit I did it). 

We made it to the Embassy at 9:45 and Andy had to make an emergency stop at the bathroom. While I was waiting on the sidewalk, I saw two motorcycles collide. Not too bad, the drivers were up and walking. When we finally got inside, they told us we had to go to an agency for the group visa. When we went to the agency, they told us to go down the street. It was a shady building, 3rd floor, not much else going on, but yeah we'll leave our visas w you. We opted for expedited service so we could get them the next day. Next was the Tourism Board for the Annapurna Circiut passes. No one there so it was easy. I love how rules are lax in these countries. Yes you need to have your passport for the pass, but it's ok if you don't. 

We walked to Durbar Square to see temples. The intricate details around the wooden doors and windows that held up over these hundred of years were amazing. Man the earthquake did a number on them. Sidewalks were shifted and torn up, some wooden pieces were gathered in an attempt to make the mess organized, but little was being done. Some walls were curving and being held up by small wooden beams w rebar staked in the ground, some temples were completely collapsed. At this pace it's going to take them a very long time to rebuild. Not many tourists. 

On our way to Harati Devi temple we saw a lot of old blood stains on the ground, probably from bike accidents. We crossed a river and it was pretty disgusting. The smells of the city were getting to me and my scarf didn't help. Smog, nasty water, deisel, poop, then a hint of food here and there. I was def not hungry. Andy navigated and I followed. Its it easy to navigate these streets, especially when there are limited street names. 


We walked up all the steps to the top of the hill to the temple and passed all the monkeys while trying to avoid the dog/monkey fights on the stairs. There were 5 or so eagles hovering around, waiting for a baby monkey to grab. There were amazing views of the city from the top. Tens of prayer flags were traversing the valley between the temples. It was beautiful. A quick tour and I was ready to head back. I needed a shower and had enough of the city for one day. 

The shower was the best thing that's happened in several days (it's the only one I've taken since we left) and it was worth it. Now I can do dinner. We walked back to Thamel and found Thamel House which a coworker recommended. We got the fixed meal, me veg and he not veg, and shared. It was a ton of food and delish. I didn't do much damage, I know I can do better. Maybe it's all the spices or the smells of the city that I need to get used to. Plus it's 6 and past our bedtime. Crossing the street at night is interesting. Just when we think we've got it down, we either stop traffic or end up running across. We hit the hay at 8. Looks like we've adjusted!
26k steps; 11 miles; 54 floors

items.title: Sitting and waiting 11/28
items.body:
We've been traveling for over 36 hours. The flight to Frankfurt was fast since we passed out the majority of the trip w a little help from our pills. I should have drugged the old ladies behind me who wouldn't shut up. 

Layover then off to Delhi. While we still slept on this 7 hr flight, I was crammed in the middle with an old lady who didn't care for personal space (welcome to India) and Andy who's knees barely fit. We landed at 1:30am and passed through customs w/ no issues. As soon as we came down the stairs for customs I could see the air. Maybe the smog leaks in the building. Plus it's hot. People have winter clothes on and I'm sweating in a Tshirt. I hope my body is prepping for the cold we are about to encounter. Another layover and off to Kathmandu. I'm amazing that my body is allowing me to do nothing but sit and sleep and eat w/o freaking out. Good thing I quit exerting before we left.

items.title: And we're off! 11/27
items.body:
I like to get to the airport early. I can't help it. I can thank my mother for that. Andy likes to do things up to the last min. He can't help it. So we left for the airport later than I wanted. It won't be busy he says. It's a low travel day he says. He was right. Walked through the gate in 15 min thanks to Precheck. 

My bag weighed a whopping 30# and his 35# which included all the school supplies. Damn maybe I should have brought more shit. Since I won't have two bags of wine this should feel like a breeze. 

Time to spare for a quick bite of Japanese since we won't be eating raw fish for a while. I got dirty looks when I hacked up my lung from the fellow restaurant patrons. I hope this is the tail end of the cold. Stress, drinking and not exercising is a great regiment in prep for a major hike. Bring on the airplane germs. 

Last night Andy suggested the $5/night hostel. F that! I'm upgrading us to the $12 room baby. Nothing but the best for us!l

Last 50 people to board and he has to go to the bathroom. Seriously dude? I'll have to adapt to looser time restrictions.  I didn't sign my passport and the dude said I wouldn't be let back into the U.S. Jeez. I wish I wanted a drink but my cold doesn't agree w that thinking- yet.
Let the Xanax consumption commence!
